title: Present Value of a Single Payment
description:
Return the present value of a single payment of `future_value` due in `years` years, discounted at the annual effective rate `interest_rate`.

$$PV = FV\,(1+i)^{-n}$$

### Function signature

```r
present_value <- function(future_value, interest_rate, years)
```

### Example

```r
> present_value(1000, 0.05, 10)
[1] 613.91
```

### Notes

- When `years` is 0 the present value equals the future value.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.

title: Crude Mortality Rate
description:


### Example

### Notes

- Use base R only (no packages).

title: Curtate Life Expectancy
description:
`lives` is a life-table column $l_0, l_1, \dots, l_\omega$: the number of survivors at successive ages, starting with the age of interest. Return the curtate expectation of life at the first age, the expected number of complete future years lived:

$$e_0 = \frac{1}{l_0}\sum_{k \ge 1} l_k$$

### Function signature

```r
life_expectancy <- function(lives)
```

### Example

```r
> life_expectancy(c(1000, 990, 980, 970))
[1] 2.94
```

### Notes

- The table ends at the last value given (everyone is dead one year later).
- If only $l_0$ is given the curtate expectation is 0.
- `lives` is a numeric vector; `lives[1]` is $l_0$.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.

$$PV = P\,a_{\overline{n}|} = P\,\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

title: Historical Value at Risk
description:
Estimate the historical Value at Risk of a return series at `confidence_level` $c$, **as a positive loss**. Sort the returns in ascending order, take the one at zero-based position $k = \lfloor (1 - c)\,n \rfloor$, and return its negative.

### Function signature

```r
value_at_risk <- function(returns, confidence_level)
```

### Example

```r
> value_at_risk(c(0.1, -0.05, 0.08, -0.02), 0.95)
[1] 0.05
```

### Notes

- A positive result is a loss; e.g. a VaR of 0.05 means a 5% loss.
- Compute $k$ exactly as stated (floor, zero-based); the tests avoid cases where rounding error matters.
- R vectors are 1-based, so the zero-based position $k$ is element `k + 1`.
- Don't name helper variables `var`: it would mask base R's `var()`.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.

title: Approximate Yield to Maturity
description:
Estimate the yield to maturity of an annual-coupon bond with the standard approximation. The annual coupon is $C = \text{coupon\_rate} \times F$, the price is $P$ and the term is $n$ years.

$$\text{YTM} \approx \frac{C + (F - P)/n}{(F + P)/2}$$

### Function signature

```r

```

### Example

title: Macaulay Duration of a Bond
description:
Return the Macaulay duration, **in years**, of a bond redeemed at `face_value` after `years` years. Coupons are paid `frequency` times a year; `coupon_rate` and `yield_rate` are nominal annual rates convertible `frequency` times a year. With $m$ = `frequency`, $j = y/m$ and cash flows $CF_k$ at periods $k = 1,\dots,mn$ (coupon $cF/m$, plus $F$ at the last period):

$$D = \frac{1}{m}\,\frac{\sum_k k\,CF_k\,(1+j)^{-k}}{\sum_k CF_k\,(1+j)^{-k}}$$

### Function signature

```r
bond_duration <- function(face_value, coupon_rate, yield_rate, years, frequency)
```

### Example

```r
> bond_duration(1000, 0.05, 0.06, 10, 2)
[1] 7.895
```

### Notes

- A zero-coupon bond has a duration equal to its term.
- `years * frequency` is a whole number of periods.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.
solution:
bond_duration <- function(face_value, coupon_rate, yield_rate, years, frequency) {
  n <- years * frequency
  k <- seq_len(n)
  j <- yield_rate / frequency
  cf <- rep(face_value * coupon_rate / frequency, n)
  cf[n] <- cf[n] + face_value
  pv <- cf / (1 + j)^k
  sum(k * pv) / sum(pv) / frequency
}

title: Policy Value by Recursion
description:
A policy pays a level annual `premium` at the start of each year and a death `benefit` at the end of the year of death. The one-year death probability `mortality_rate` and the interest rate `interest_rate` are the same every year. Starting from ${}_0V = 0$, roll the policy value forward with the recursion

$${}_{t+1}V = \frac{\left({}_tV + P\right)(1+i) - q\,S}{1 - q}$$

and return ${}_tV$ after `years_elapsed` years.

### Function signature

```r
reserve <- function(premium, benefit, mortality_rate, interest_rate, years_elapsed)
```

### Example

```r
> reserve(1000, 100000, 0.01, 0.05, 5)
[1] 285.05
```

### Notes

- After 0 years the policy value is 0.
- A negative value is possible when premiums are too low for the risk.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.

title: Term Assurance Net Single Premium
description:

$$NSP = S \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} v^{k+1}\,{}_kp_x\,q_{x+k}$$

### Function signature

```r
net_single_premium <- function(sum_assured, age, mortality_table, interest_rate, term)
```

### Example

```r
> net_single_premium(100000, 30, list("30" = 0.001, "31" = 0.0012, "32" = 0.0014), 0.05, 3)
[1] 324.64
```

### Notes

- With `term = 0` there is no cover and the premium is 0.
- In R the table arrives as a named list, e.g. `list("30" = 0.001, "31" = 0.0012)`; look ages up with `mortality_table[[as.character(age + k)]]`.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.

title: Internal Rate of Return (Newton-Raphson)
description:
`cash_flows[t]` is the net cash flow at time $t = 0, 1, \dots$ Find the internal rate of return, the rate $r$ with $NPV(r) = 0$, using Newton-Raphson iteration from `initial_guess`:

$$NPV(r) = \sum_t \frac{CF_t}{(1+r)^t}, \qquad NPV'(r) = -\sum_t \frac{t\,CF_t}{(1+r)^{t+1}}, \qquad r \leftarrow r - \frac{NPV(r)}{NPV'(r)}$$

Stop when the step is smaller than $10^{-10}$ in absolute value, or after 100 iterations.

### Function signature

```r
irr <- function(cash_flows, initial_guess)
```

### Example

```r
> irr(c(-1000, 300, 300, 300, 300), 0.1)
[1] 0.0771385
```

### Notes

- The tests use conventional cash flows (one outflow, then inflows), which have a single IRR.
- Cash flows are 0-indexed in time: element 1 of the vector is the flow at $t = 0$.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.

title: Bond Convexity
description:
Return the convexity, **in years squared**, of a bond redeemed at `face_value` after `years` years with coupons paid `frequency` times a year (`coupon_rate` and `yield_rate` are nominal annual rates convertible `frequency` times a year). With $m$ = `frequency`, $j = y/m$, cash flows $CF_k$ at periods $k = 1,\dots,mn$ and price $P = \sum_k CF_k (1+j)^{-k}$:

$$C = \frac{1}{P\,m^2\,(1+j)^2}\sum_{k} k(k+1)\,CF_k\,(1+j)^{-k}$$

### Function signature

```r
convexity <- function(face_value, coupon_rate, yield_rate, years, frequency)
```

### Example

```r
> convexity(1000, 0.05, 0.06, 10, 2)
[1] 71.7854
```

### Notes

- Dividing by $m^2$ converts from periods squared to years squared.
- For a zero-coupon bond with annual compounding, $C = n(n+1)/(1+y)^2$.
- Use base R only (no packages).
- Don't round your result: example outputs are rounded for display, and answers are accepted within 0.5%.
solution:
convexity <- function(face_value, coupon_rate, yield_rate, years, frequency) {
  n <- years * frequency
  k <- seq_len(n)
  j <- yield_rate / frequency
  cf <- rep(face_value * coupon_rate / frequency, n)
  cf[n] <- cf[n] + face_value
  pv <- cf / (1 + j)^k
  sum(k * (k + 1) * pv) / (sum(pv) * frequency^2 * (1 + j)^2)
}
